task_text: Open Door: A free-standing door stands ahead of the hovering aerial manipulator: an oak door panel in a metal frame, hinged on its left edge (as seen from the robot), with a metal lever handle near its right edge on the robot-facing side. Open the door: swing the panel on its hinge, away from the robot, by more than 20 degrees from closed. Success: Success when the revolute joint Hinge has position > 20 degrees = 0.349066 rad (door_opened_threshold_deg; strict inequality). The joint ranges from 0 rad (closed, its value at every reset) to pi/2 rad; positive is the panel's rotation about the vertical hinge axis that swings its free edge away from the robot. Nothing else is checked (the robot need not pass through the doorway). AM-Bench also reports subtask criteria door_engaged (joint position >= 0.05 x 0.349066 = 0.017453 rad) and door_opened (the success condition); they are informational only. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 15 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 1800 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 1799th step.
episode: one episode, no reset: it ends at the first control step where AM-Bench's success check holds, when the task's episode length of 15 s of simulated time runs out (AM-Bench's time-out, at control step 1799), when your time is up, or on a simulator error; the simulated clock advances only with the control steps you run
